speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you are experiencing right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and cognitive changes like forgetfulness and paranoia. Can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting progressively worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent head trauma or infections, and do you have a history of seizures or abnormal movements like twitching? I also need to know if you have had any recent weight loss or changes in sleep patterns.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the somnolence, confusion, and non-enhancing white matter lesions with a high viral load, I suspect HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) or possibly toxoplasmosis despite the lack of enhancement. DIAGNOSIS READY: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder
